newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen fragile, Dow lends support.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen fragile, Dow lends support.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen fragile on Wednesday although a sharp rally in the Dow Jones on Tuesday could lend psychological support, dealers said.
"The market will take its first cues from the Wall Street rally," a local brokerage dealer said.
The Dow Jones index surged 173.38 points to its second largest advance in its history at 6,833.59.
Selective buying of heavily sold Singapore stocks could help the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stay afloat but sentiment was still seen weak due to slow economic recovery.
On Tuesday, the STII closed up 9.67 points at 2,047.56.
The UOB OTC index measuring mostly Malaysian over the counter stocks dropped 12.38 points to 1,176.87.
Volatility in Malaysian stocks would continue to drain market liquidity, dealers said.
